The foundational operators—rolling EPA, trust profiles, and TWP-based INT projections—are unified through temporal and probabilistic inference layers. Rolling EPA provides dynamic performance context, trust profiles encode receiver-specific reliability under uncertainty, and TWP projections refine risk modeling. These primitives form a coherent system where trust deltas adjust based on availability, while INT projections update under changing turnover dynamics. Dualities emerge between form and function: EPA reflects form, trust encodes functional dependency, and INT projections quantify risk. Failure modes include data sparsity in small samples, misalignment between charting and actual performance, and overfitting to historical turnover patterns. Each operator must be validated against permuted-label nulls to ensure statistical significance.
